paper_title: Monopole-vortex continuity of N = 1 super Yang-Mills theory on R^2 x S^1 x S^1 with 't Hooft twist (Hayashi, 2025, JHEP)
core_reasoning_3:
\textbf{Claim.} Let \(\omega:=e^{2\pi i/N}\). If the Polyakov-loop basis \(\{|m\rangle:m\in\mathbb Z_N\}\) satisfies
\[
P_2|m\rangle=\omega^m|m\rangle,
\]
and the center-vortex contribution to \(\mathcal O:=\operatorname{tr}(\lambda\lambda)\) shifts \(|m\rangle\) to \(|m+1\rangle\) with amplitude \(A\), then the Fourier states
\[
|f_k\rangle:=\frac{1}{\sqrt N}\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z_N}\omega^{-km}|m\rangle
\]
diagonalize \(\mathcal O\), with eigenvalue \(A\omega^k\), and the low-energy operators obey
\[
\mathcal O P_2=\omega^{-1}P_2\mathcal O.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
(P1)\quad & N\geq2,\quad \omega:=e^{2\pi i/N},\quad \mathbb Z_N:=\{0,1,\ldots,N-1\}\text{ with indices mod }N.\\
(P2)\quad & P_2|m\rangle=\omega^m|m\rangle\quad (m\in\mathbb Z_N).\\
(P3)\quad & \mathcal O|m\rangle=A|m+1\rangle\quad (m\in\mathbb Z_N),\quad A\in\mathbb C.\\
(P4)\quad & |f_k\rangle:=\frac{1}{\sqrt N}\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z_N}\omega^{-km}|m\rangle\quad (k\in\mathbb Z_N).\\
(P5)\quad & \omega^m\omega^{-km}=\omega^{-(k-1)m},\quad \omega^{-k(n-1)}=\omega^k\omega^{-kn}.\\
(P6)\quad & \omega^N=1,\quad \omega\neq0.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
First apply \(\mathcal O\) to the Fourier state:
\begin{align*}
\mathcal O|f_k\rangle
&=\mathcal O\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt N}\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z_N}\omega^{-km}|m\rangle\right) && \text{by (P4)}\\
&=\frac{1}{\sqrt N}\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z_N}\omega^{-km}\mathcal O|m\rangle && \text{linearity}\\
&=\frac{A}{\sqrt N}\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z_N}\omega^{-km}|m+1\rangle && \text{by (P3)}.
\end{align*}
Set \(n:=m+1\). Since the indices are modulo \(N\), the sum over \(m\in\mathbb Z_N\) equals the sum over \(n\in\mathbb Z_N\). Hence
\begin{align*}
\mathcal O|f_k\rangle
&=\frac{A}{\sqrt N}\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z_N}\omega^{-k(n-1)}|n\rangle && \text{substitute }m=n-1\\
&=\frac{A\omega^k}{\sqrt N}\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z_N}\omega^{-kn}|n\rangle && \text{by (P5)}\\
&=A\omega^k|f_k\rangle. && \text{by (P4)}
\end{align*}
Thus \(|f_k\rangle\) diagonalizes \(\mathcal O\). Next compute the operator product on \(|m\rangle\):
\begin{align*}
\mathcal O P_2|m\rangle
&=\mathcal O(\omega^m|m\rangle) && \text{by (P2)}\\
&=\omega^m A|m+1\rangle && \text{by (P3)},\\
P_2\mathcal O|m\rangle
&=P_2(A|m+1\rangle) && \text{by (P3)}\\
&=A\omega^{m+1}|m+1\rangle && \text{by (P2)}\\
&=\omega\,A\omega^m|m+1\rangle. && \text{algebra}
\end{align*}
Therefore
\begin{align*}
P_2\mathcal O|m\rangle&=\omega\,\mathcal O P_2|m\rangle && \text{compare previous two lines}\\
\mathcal O P_2|m\rangle&=\omega^{-1}P_2\mathcal O|m\rangle && \text{multiply by }\omega^{-1}.
\end{align*}
Because this holds for every basis vector \(|m\rangle\), it holds as an operator identity on the low-energy Hilbert space.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\mathcal O|f_k\rangle=Ae^{2\pi i k/N}|f_k\rangle,\qquad \mathcal O P_2=e^{-2\pi i/N}P_2\mathcal O.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
